articles.why: The text has changed since your review of 2026-10-18: recheck your findings, then review the rest.

recheck.issue: Effective permissions depend on the agent's configured identity and how it is invoked: in chat with User's account, the requester's; in automation, the connection account's, which need not be the rule's creator or the agent's creator; with Agent's account, the agent's own. 'Typically whoever created the rule' implies more than Atlassian documents.
recheck.quote: Some paths run as somebody else. When a Rovo agent runs from Jira Automation, it uses the permissions of the automation's connection user, typically whoever created the rule
recheck.note: The identity point is rewritten around Atlassian's identity setting: the requester in chat, the connection account in automation (quoting ROVO-837's 'always use the permissions of the connection user in the automation', since the support-article sentence the review quoted was not found), or the agent's own account; the agent's creator is named as not the deciding identity.

recheck.issue: ROVO-837 documents disclosure of a restricted page reference in an automation's output; opening the link still failed. It does not show access to the page or its full content. The reporter notes it does not occur in Rovo Chat.
recheck.quote: links to pages the triggering user cannot view
recheck.note: Now says the case disclosed a link to a restricted page, not the page; the link still failed; reading with one identity and publishing to a wider audience is the risk.

recheck.issue: Atlassian now documents agents with their own accounts; its 6 October announcement still lists wider agent-account controls and a non-human identity inventory as coming. Availability should be checked per tenant. Agent's-account agents also make content shared with them available to their users.
recheck.note: Agent accounts described as documented, with the 6 October announcement quoted for the wider controls, a check-your-tenant line, and Atlassian's warning that content shared with such an agent is shared with its users.

recheck.issue: The file was less discoverable, not safe; Drive sharing settings still apply.
recheck.quote: was safe while nobody knew the link
recheck.note: Now 'hard to find', with 'Google Drive sharing settings still apply.'

recheck.issue: True of Google Drive, not of every connector: synced, direct and Smart Link connectors differ in setup, indexing and authentication.
recheck.quote: Connectors are set up by an administrator with broad rights, and then each user links their own account
recheck.note: Now distinguishes synced, direct and Smart Link connectors, quoting Atlassian's connector types page.

recheck.issue: Restricting who creates agents (by group) and who uses a particular agent (individuals only) are different controls.
recheck.quote: administrators can narrow it to selected groups
recheck.note: Creation by group and use by individual are now separate, with Atlassian's sentence on group restriction not being supported.

recheck.issue: Audit logs record events; they do not prevent them. Classification identifies sensitivity and bounds only through a policy acting on it. Only blocking and redaction can prevent data moving.
recheck.quote: classification, redaction of sensitive data and audit logs, sit in the boundary row too
recheck.note: The governance tools are now sorted by what each does: blocking and redaction can bound, classification only through a policy, audit logs are evidence, not a barrier.

recheck.issue: Indexing allowlists control indexing, not everything Rovo can fetch at run time with the user's access; MCP server permissions govern that server's operations, not every Rovo path, on Atlassian's documentation.
recheck.quote: The administrator's allowlists for which drives and sites are indexed
recheck.note: The allowlists are scoped to indexing, and the MCP switches to what the MCP server does, as Atlassian's page states.

recheck.issue: The PromptArmor report is accurate as a historical report; present exploitability is unverified.
recheck.quote: I found no statement from Atlassian on a fix
recheck.note: Now dated, described as reported as of publication, with current exploitability marked unverified, here and in the limits.

recheck.issue: No population evidence for the size of the gap or how often controls are only prompt instructions.
recheck.quote: for most organisations that is most of the company
recheck.note: Now 'It can be large, and it has to be measured for the particular deployment rather than assumed'; the earlier 'most organisations' and 'almost nobody' wording is softened.

recheck.issue: The library is example policies; connectors to customer systems are built per engagement and none is a product yet.
recheck.note: Now 'policies for commercial agents', with RiskMandate's own sentence that no connector is a product yet.

recheck.issue: The pricing page marks the £500 and £1,500 levels specified, never run, as of 15 September 2026.
recheck.quote: from £10 for the pack to £1,500 reviewed
recheck.note: Now quotes the pricing page's 'specified, never run' for the top two levels, and adds it to the limits.

recheck.issue: The merged page documents an external adapter governed by a pinned copy of the evaluator; it does not alter Ruflo's running policy or restrict other shell or MCP tools.
recheck.quote: enforced it in Ruflo's evaluator, in real time, on every memory operation
recheck.note: Now scoped to the memory operations of the external adapter, with the page's own statement of what it does not change.

recheck.issue: The Northstar results come from a scripted simulation with synthetic cases and no model.
recheck.quote: overpays $458 in a day; the design with three policies gets all thirteen right
recheck.note: Now 'thirteen synthetic refund requests', 'a scripted simulation: invented orders, scripted mistakes, no model called', and what it does and does not show.

recheck.issue: The Code applies to specified listed companies, not every UK board.
recheck.quote: Under the UK Corporate Governance Code, boards already have to determine the principal risks
recheck.note: Now 'For companies the UK Corporate Governance Code applies to'.
